chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: The Hambone hit
summary: Saunders turned a children's song into Hambone for Okeh around 1952; covers followed by Tommy Dorsey, Tennessee Ernie and Jo Stafford, and Leon Washington arranged it.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. How did that come about?
That was quite a hit. 'Hambone, hambone.' That's an old children's song, isn't it?

It was a -- that's what it was. I saw these children singing this thing, and doing the thing, and so we set and put it together, and then I called they guy who we were recording for at that time, for Okeh, and he come in and he heard this thing and he flipped over it. So then we recorded it. And it really, really caught on. Then I had about six records on it, that that time, Tommy Dorsey --

Right, that was the early -- about '52. And then -- '51 or '52, what's his name, Tommy Dorsey recorded it, and what's his name sang it, Charlie Shavers, yeah, and then Tennessee Ernie had a record on it, and Jo Stafford had a record, and those --
Right, we got everything from it, yeah. So Leon Washington and I -- do you remember Leon?
He did the arrangements for it, right.
